name: multi-select
purpose: Editable combobox with a multi-selectable listbox (WAI-ARIA 1.2): selected values appear as chips with remove buttons, typing filters (or loads) options, activating an option toggles it, and an optional Select all and maximum help larger choices.
whenToUse: Choosing several values from a list long enough to benefit from filtering (roughly 7+ options).
Tags, skills, recipients, or teams from a known (or searchable) set.
whenNotToUse: A few options that fit on screen: use Checkbox Group.
One value: use Combobox or Select.
Free-text tags that are not in a list (custom values are not supported).
responsive: The control is full width of its container and wraps chips onto new lines; the listbox matches the control width, flips above when space below is insufficient, and caps its height to the available space and the popover-max-height token.
rtl: Logical properties; popup alignment honours the `direction` option/configuration.
theme: Control surface, chip, selected, hover, and focus tokens. Selection is shown with a check mark and aria-selected, not color alone; the active option uses an outline. Forced-colors mode uses Highlight/HighlightText and CanvasText boundaries.
security: Option and chip labels are rendered with textContent; loaded options are validated as untrusted data. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence or telemetry. With loadOptions the consumer performs requests. With `name`, one hidden input per selected value carries it for form submission.

performance.testedScale: 1,000 options; larger lists should use loadOptions (no virtualization).

limitations: Strict selection: values are always options; free text is never a value and is cleared when focus leaves.
No virtualization: all filtered options are rendered.
Chip remove buttons are in the tab order (one stop per selected value); Backspace in the empty input removes the last value.
Select all acts on the options shown (after filtering or loading), up to maxSelected.
unsupported: Option values that are not strings.
antiPatterns: Very small option sets better served by checkboxes.
